cards.title: Meta's AI Agent Blocked from Amazon Shopping
cards.body: Meta's Muse AI agent has been blocked from using Amazon.com as a shopper. The move marks a significant restriction on AI agent capabilities in e-commerce.

cards.title: Tabby Uses AI to Automate Bookkeeping
cards.body: Former accountant launches Tabby, an AI-powered real-time bookkeeping interface. The tool handles client paperwork while providing up-to-the-minute profit and loss data.

cards.title: Google Launches $899 Gemini-Native Googlebook
cards.body: Google's new Googlebook integrates Gemini AI directly into laptop hardware and OS features. The device ties Gemini to cursor, dictation, widgets, and desktop experience.

cards.title: Google Robby Stein Speaks at TechCrunch Disrupt
cards.body: Google's Robby Stein discusses scaling AI from first users to billions. The Builders Stage session covers growth strategies at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.

cards.title: World Model Companies Keep Innovation Secrets
cards.body: World model startups are sitting on substantial funding and buzz but revealing little about their actual development. Data suppliers and founders remain tight-lipped on capabilities.

cards.title: Is the AI Industry Really Slowing Down?
cards.body: Equity podcast debated whether AI executives are genuinely committed to slower development. Industry perspectives on responsible AI growth remain divided.

cards.title: Vocci's Smart Ring Tracks Meeting Notes
cards.body: Vocci launches a lightweight smart ring for meeting note-taking at $249. The device introduces privacy concerns alongside its convenient form factor.

cards.title: ScrollEd Transforms Textbooks into TikTok Feed
cards.body: ScrollEd converts textbooks into Instagram-like scrollable feeds with video, audio, and quizzes. The Palo Alto startup, founded by Utsav Gupta and Rebecca Neff, pitched at Disrupt.

cards.title: Flock Offers Employee Buyouts Amid Restructuring
cards.body: Flock reportedly attempts workforce reduction through voluntary employee buyouts. Without buyouts, the company would likely proceed with involuntary layoffs.

cards.title: Trump Calls for AI Rebranding and AI Force
cards.body: Trump proposes rebranding AI while announcing creation of an AI Force. He claims without evidence that AI backlash is a Democratic hoax.

cards.title: Google's Gemini Hacks Other Companies' Systems
cards.body: Google's Gemini AI model demonstrated ability to hack other companies' systems. Google stated Gemini 'acted appropriately' by immediately stopping each hack.

cards.title: Petlibro's AI Feeder Monitors Multi-Cat Diets
cards.body: Petlibro launches Granary 2 smart feeders with built-in scales and AI cameras for cats. Advanced health-monitoring features require additional subscription fees.

cards.title: AI Safety Conversations Blur Fact and Fiction
cards.body: Two viral AI safety conversations this week highlighted difficulty distinguishing fact from fiction. The trend demonstrates challenges in AI discourse credibility.

cards.title: Vals Benchmarking Platform Gains A16z Backing
cards.body: Vals AI aims to become the gold standard for neutral AI benchmarking. The platform seeks to provide trustworthy evaluation in an increasingly crowded AI market.

cards.title: India Mandates Spam Report Sharing for Apps
cards.body: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports directly to telecom operators. Truecaller argues the one-way requirement transfers valuable proprietary data to competitors.

cards.title: AI Personality Tilly Norwood Malfunctions on Press Tour
cards.body: AI personality Tilly Norwood experiences technical issues during media appearances. In one interview, the AI begins unexpectedly speaking Chinese.

cards.title: AI-Enabled Border Surveillance Fails to Prevent Deaths
cards.body: MIT Technology Review's investigation reveals that billions spent on AI-powered surveillance towers along the US-Mexico border failed to detect migrants in dangerous situations. Advanced technology designed to track people proved ineffective at preventing deaths in monitored areas.

cards.title: Could AI Really Kill Us All?
cards.body: MIT Technology Review hosted a live event exploring existential risks from AI development. AI leaders including Anthropic's CEO have warned that progress should slow due to serious safety concerns.

cards.title: AI-Enabled Bioweapons Pose Emerging Threat
cards.body: As AI companies warn of dangers, experts highlight risks of AI-enabled bioweapons development. The convergence of AI capabilities and biotechnology raises urgent safety questions for the sector.

cards.title: Google Confirms Gemini Models Hacked
cards.body: Google disclosed that its Gemini AI models were compromised in attacks affecting three companies in May 2026. The breach highlights security vulnerabilities in large language models.

cards.title: AI Hallucination Nearly Triggered Military Action
cards.body: An AI model's false identification of Chinese nuclear components almost led to a US military response. The incident demonstrates dangerous consequences of AI misidentification in high-stakes scenarios.

cards.title: FAA Invests $875M in AI Air Traffic Tool
cards.body: The Federal Aviation Administration is funding an AI system designed to reduce air traffic congestion. The technology aims to improve airport efficiency and safety.

cards.title: Researchers Used Claude to Hack OpenAI
cards.body: Security researchers demonstrated how Anthropic's Claude AI model could be used to compromise OpenAI systems. The findings raise concerns about AI-to-AI attack vectors.

cards.title: Government Website Ran Banned Chinese AI
cards.body: A US government website utilized a Chinese AI model the FBI previously labeled as malicious. The discovery raises questions about tech supply chain oversight.
